name: Comprehensive Certificate in Finance
description: University-benchmarked finance breadth fused with 2026 job-market requirements across corporate finance, FP&A, valuation, capital allocation, markets/risk, finance data and governed AI-enabled decision systems.
university_benchmark: Wharton Finance | MIT Sloan Finance | Yale Financial Markets | Chicago Booth Finance

courses.title: Financial Modeling, Business Cases & Unit Economics
Valuation, cost of capital + capital structure

capstone: Act as finance lead for a real or simulated business unit. Reconcile historical financial statements and operating data; build a 12-18 month driver-based operating forecast with P&L, cash-flow and working-capital logic; complete a month-end variance bridge; model base/upside/downside scenarios; evaluate one investment or strategic choice using NPV/IRR/DCF/returns; assess capital structure and risk where relevant; query and reconcile source data in SQL; publish a finance KPI dashboard; automate one recurring finance workflow with traceability, exception handling and human approval; finish with a CFO memo and board-style recommendation.
evidence_standard: Every student-facing resource on the Finance certificate is a full university lecture/masterclass or substantial expert webinar/recording. No syllabus pages, registration-only pages or low-value short explainers are used as learner bridges.

name: Comprehensive Certificate in Business Administration
description: A modern general-management certificate that integrates finance, marketing, analytics, strategy, operations, leadership, negotiation, planning and AI-era business transformation into one execution-oriented management spine.
university_benchmark: Harvard Business School | Wharton | Stanford GSB | Chicago Booth | Yale SOM

courses.title: Market Research, Competitive Analysis & Market Sizing

capstone: Run a simulated business unit through a full operating cycle. Define the market/customer problem and strategic choices; build a simple business and financial model; set 12-month priorities, budget and resource allocation; create a KPI tree plus weekly/monthly/quarterly operating cadence; design a pricing/GTM plan; map and improve one core process; assign cross-functional roles and decision rights; negotiate one contested resource or stakeholder decision; create a people/change plan; redesign one recurring workflow with AI using value, risk, human-control and adoption criteria; then deliver an executive quarterly review that reallocates resources based on evidence.
evidence_standard: Every student-facing resource on the Business Administration certificate is a substantial university lecture/masterclass or recorded expert session. Ivy League content is included through Harvard PON, while Booth, MIT, Stanford, OpenAI and recognized strategy experts provide complementary depth. No curriculum pages or quick explainer videos are used as learner bridges.

courses.title: Executive Presence & Speaking to Senior Leaders

name: Comprehensive Certificate in Entrepreneurship
description: A founder-operator certificate for taking a venture from problem discovery through product-market fit, first revenue, financing and scale - with rigorous customer evidence, founder-led selling, unit economics, negotiation, operating systems and AI-native opportunity judgment.
university_benchmark: Harvard Innovation Labs / HBS | Stanford STVP / GSB | MIT Sloan | Wharton Entrepreneurship

courses.title: Financial Modeling, Business Cases & Unit Economics

capstone: Launch and operate a venture through an evidence-based founder cycle. Interview at least 15 target customers; define a beachhead segment and value proposition; prototype an MVP and run usability/demand tests; win or simulate a credible path to the first five customers; build pricing, revenue model, unit economics and 18-month cash/runway scenarios; create a founder-led GTM and growth experiment backlog; form the company structure and key founder/partner terms; prepare a financing strategy and investor data room; build hiring/culture/decision mechanisms for the next stage; identify one AI-native product or operating advantage and test its economics, reliability and trust risks; finish with a board/investor update showing traction, learning, risks and the next scale/pivot/stop decision.
evidence_standard: Every Entrepreneurship bridge is a full workshop, lecture or complete founder/operator talk from Harvard, MIT, Stanford or Y Combinator. The set intentionally favors 45-90+ minute resources and excludes curriculum pages, registration-only pages and low-value short explainers.
